findings.evidence: "Similarly, the IT asset group tracks the stipend budget each quarter."
findings.fix: Either remove "Similarly" and present this as an unrelated fact, or explain how IT asset tracking relates to the reimbursement log.
findings.violation: "Similarly" implies parallelism with the prior sentence about publishing the reimbursement log, but budget tracking by a different team is not actually similar or related; the connector misleads about the relationship between the two facts.

findings.evidence: "If the position counts as full-time, the stipend can apply. If the employee has completed 90 days of continuous service, the stipend can apply. If the request arrives before the benefit year ends, the stipend can apply. Only once every condition above is met does the home-office equipment stipend become available"
findings.fix: Rewrite as a single compound condition, e.g., "The stipend is available only if the position is full-time, the employee has completed 90 days of continuous service, and the request arrives before the benefit year ends."
findings.violation: Each conditional sentence individually implies that satisfying that one condition alone makes the stipend applicable ("can apply"), which directly contradicts the closing sentence stating all three conditions must be met together.

findings.fix: Change to "If the employee's position is full-time."
findings.violation: "The position" has no antecedent in the document - it's unclear whose position this refers to (presumably the requesting employee's), creating ambiguity.

findings.evidence: "Then, the review takes longer because the manager who normally handles it is traveling; the backup reviewer who covers for absences was not told that the request needs sign-off before the portal releases the confirmation email."
findings.fix: Remove this sentence, or replace it with a general policy statement (e.g., how backup reviewers are notified when a primary approver is unavailable).
findings.violation: This reads as a narrative account of a specific past incident/failure rather than a general policy or procedural rule, and it doesn't belong in a section meant to describe how to apply.

findings.evidence: "the review takes longer because the manager who normally handles it is traveling" (How to Apply) vs. "The request is reviewed within two business days" (Approval Timeline)
findings.fix: Reconcile the sections, e.g., state the two-day SLA and explicitly note exceptions (such as reviewer absence) and how they're handled.
findings.location: How to Apply vs. Approval Timeline
findings.violation: The two sections give contradictory expectations about review speed - one describes an indefinite delay, the other promises a fixed two-day turnaround.

findings.evidence: "The manager approves items pursuant to internal discretion, notwithstanding the standard review checklist."
findings.fix: Clarify explicitly, e.g., "The manager approves items using the standard review checklist; exceptions require documented justification."
findings.violation: This sentence is self-contradictory/unclear - it's not stated whether the checklist governs approval or the manager's discretion overrides it, and it conflicts with Approval Timeline's statement that "the manager confirms the equipment category matches the approved list," which implies an objective standard.

findings.evidence: "the deposit happens in order to offset costs the employee already paid at this point in time"
findings.fix: Simplify to "The deposit reimburses costs the employee has already paid."
findings.violation: Circular, overly wordy phrasing that says little more than "reimburses costs already paid"; "at this point in time" is filler.

findings.evidence: "You must keep your equipment in good working condition and we may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.fix: Rewrite in third person, e.g., "Employees must keep equipment in good working condition, and the benefits team may request a brief photo check once a year."
findings.violation: This switches to second-person ("You"/"we") while the rest of the document uses third person ("the employee," "the manager"), creating an inconsistent voice.

findings.evidence: "Similarly, the policy applies to one device per category per employee."
findings.fix: Remove "Similarly" or replace with a neutral transition like "Additionally."
findings.violation: "Similarly" falsely implies this rule is parallel to the preceding photo-check requirement, but it's an unrelated restriction (device limits vs. condition/verification).

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the stipend item against the request log each month. Payroll releases the stipend item amount after that monthly review."
findings.fix: Rename the section to reflect its actual content (e.g., "Reconciliation Process") or add actual term definitions; vary phrasing to avoid repeating "stipend item"; use consistent third-person voice.
findings.violation: The heading "Terminology Notes" promises definitions of terms, but no terminology is actually defined; the paragraph also repeats "stipend item" three times in a stilted, redundant way, and switches to second person ("You") inconsistent with the rest of the document.

findings.evidence: "Payroll releases the stipend item amount after that monthly review" (Terminology Notes) vs. "The finance office deposits the amount within one pay cycle" (Reimbursement Amounts)
findings.fix: State a single consistent disbursement process and timeline in one place, and reference it elsewhere rather than restating it differently.
findings.violation: These two sections give conflicting accounts of who disburses the funds (payroll vs. finance office) and when (after monthly review vs. within one pay cycle).

findings.evidence: "Also, you submit the request in the portal. You track its status there until the payment clears."
findings.fix: Remove this duplicate content or merge it into the "How to Apply" section.
findings.violation: This duplicates content already covered in "How to Apply" ("Employees start a stipend request in the benefits portal"), adding redundancy without new information, and again uses inconsistent second-person voice.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt."
findings.fix: Either remove this section as redundant, or expand it into a complete, accurate step-by-step list and remove the duplicated info elsewhere.
findings.violation: This section is a thin, redundant restatement of steps already described in "How to Apply" and omits actual subsequent steps (portal submission, manager approval, payment), making it both duplicative and incomplete as a "steps" list.

findings.evidence: "## Overview" (appearing after "## Program Overview" earlier in the document)
findings.fix: Merge the two sections into one "Program Overview" section, or rename the second heading to reflect distinct content.
findings.violation: Two differently-worded headings ("Program Overview" and "Overview") both introduce overview-type content, creating structural confusion about whether they are the same section or distinct topics.

findings.evidence: "The benefits team publishes the reimbursement log after every open enrollment period."
findings.fix: State once, consistently, who publishes the reimbursement log and on what schedule.
findings.violation: This directly contradicts the earlier "Program Overview" statement that "The people operations office publishes the reimbursement log each quarter" - different owning team and different publication trigger/frequency for the same document.

findings.evidence: "The team then routes the request to the correct approver based on department."
findings.fix: Reconcile the two descriptions of how approvers are determined into one consistent process.
findings.violation: This description of approval routing (department-based) is inconsistent with "How to Apply," which describes routing to "the manager who normally handles it" and a "backup reviewer," with no mention of department-based routing.

findings.evidence: "The finance office reviews every stipend request over 200 dollars before it pays out."
findings.fix: Integrate the finance review step and its effect on timeline into the "Approval Timeline" section.
findings.violation: This additional review step and dollar threshold are never mentioned in "Approval Timeline," which describes only a two-business-day manager review - leaving the actual end-to-end timeline for requests over $200 undefined and inconsistent between sections.

findings.evidence: "The finance office also flags any request that repeats within the same quarter."
findings.fix: Align all restriction timeframes to a single consistent period (e.g., benefit year) or explicitly explain why "quarter" differs from the other limits.
findings.violation: This uses "quarter" as the relevant time window for repeat-request flagging, while the related device-limit restriction ("one device per category per employee" in Restrictions and Exceptions) and the stipend cap ("per benefit year" in Reimbursement Amounts) use different, unreconciled time units, making it unclear how these limits interact.

findings.evidence: "## Questions and Updates" heading followed by "The benefits team publishes the vendor list each quarter."
findings.fix: Rename the heading to something like "Vendor List" or add actual content about how employees can ask questions or receive policy updates.
findings.violation: The heading promises information about asking questions or receiving updates, but the content is only about vendor list publication, which doesn't match the heading.
